_comment: 英文覆盖层：按索引对齐 foods/scenes/unis 的中文条目（本文件数组顺序必须与 zh 文件一致）。覆盖 desc/history 叙述字段；名称用各条目已有的 en 字段。
history: The Taipei basin was home of the Ketagalan people; the Qing set up Taipei Prefecture and the walled city was completed in 1884, soon replacing Tainan as Taiwan's political center. Japanese-era baroque planning widened the streets; after 1945 it became the provincial capital. Taipei 101 long held 'world's tallest'; the National Palace Museum keeps 690,000+ relics from Beijing's palace; Shilin Night Market's oyster omelets and bubble tea smell worldwide. Sunsets on the Tamsui River, Beitou hot springs and Yangmingshan cherry blossoms warm this city of mountains and rivers.
importance: Provincial capital of Taiwan · Political, economic and cultural center
unis: Taiwan's oldest and largest comprehensive university — from the Taipei Imperial University, famous for its palm avenue.
The island's top teachers college — its Chinese-language center is world-known.
Taiwan's first technological university, strong in engineering.
From Nanjing's central party school — strong in humanities, media and politics.
Yangming campus famed for medicine and life sciences; merged with Chiao Tung in 2021.
A public university of law and commerce traditions — from Chung Hsing's law college.
A century-old engineering school from the Governor's industrial school.
A Catholic university founded in Beijing in 1925, re-established in Taiwan in 1961 — known for languages and communication.
Taiwan's first private university — sunset over the Taiwan Strait from Tamsui campus.
From Soochow University — law education tops the island.
A journalism and communication school — cradle of Taiwan's media people.
Design school of international fame — the fashion-show graduation is an annual event.
The first Asian university accredited by MSCHE — highly international.
A university on Yangmingshan — once the most departments on the island.
foods: Bubble tea, invented in the 1980s — one cup in every hand; chewy pearls, rich milk tea.
King of night markets! Oysters in sweet-potato batter with greens, sweet-sour sauce on top.
The Beef Noodle Festival bred countless famous shops — braised vs clear, each with fans.
Din Tai Fung's 18-fold xiaolongbao became a world brand — 'open a window, sip the soup'.
Sticky rice sausage wrapped around a Taiwan sausage — the night-market queue king.
Braised pork over hot rice with a braised egg — Taiwan's national comfort food.
Raohe market's Fuzhou pepper buns — baked in a clay oven, scalding and fragrant.
Thick bread hollowed, fried, filled with chicken-liver seafood soup — scary name, amazing taste.
Golden pineapple-cake bricks — Taipei's top souvenir.
Yongkang Street's mango shaved ice sparked an island ice war — summer sweetness.
scenes: The 508-meter bamboo-shaped tower, once the world's tallest — see all the city from floor 89.
690,000 relics — the Jadeite Cabbage and Meat-shaped Stone are the stars.
Blue-tile white-wall octagon; the hourly guard ceremony is solemn and fun.
Taipei's largest night market — from oyster omelets to 'frog eggs' drinks.
The Japanese-era hot-spring town — steaming geothermal valley and a wooden green library.
Volcanic national park — cherry trails in spring, silvergrass seas in autumn.
Fort San Domingo saw 400 years; Fisherman's Wharf's Lover Bridge sunset is famous.
A century of commerce and street culture — cinema street and the Red House.
Twenty minutes up — the Six Boulders, best photo of Taipei 101.
A temple of 1805, honored with a UNESCO heritage award.
